newsitem.title: CHINA: China B share markets up, A share indices down.
newsitem.headline: China B share markets up, A share indices down.

text.p: China's hard currency B share markets rose on Tuesday, driven by the healthy performance of a newly listed firm in Shanghai and technical factors in Shenzhen, brokers said.
But domestic currency A shares in both Shanghai and Shenzhen fell slightly on Tuesday, they said.

Shanghai's foreign currency B shares closed slightly higher on Tuesday, buoyed by the performance of Shanghai Zhenhua Port Machinery Co Ltd. The company's newly listed shares ended at $0.480 compared with an offer price of $0.433.
The Shanghai B share index gained 0.097 points or 0.13 percent to 74.481 points on volume of 24.349 million shares worth $9.104.

Zhenhua Port led the active list with 10.876 million shares changing hands. The company, which makes port handling equipment, issued 100 million B shares in mid-July to raise net proceeds of $41.135 million.
Brokers said the solid performance of the newcomer gave the market a boost, but many investors were waiting to see whether the stock could hold onto its gains in the coming days.
Despite the slight rise in the index, losers outnumbered gainers. Of 46 B shares issues, 39 traded with 17 losing ground and 15 advancing. Seven were unchanged.
Shanghai's domestic currency A shares fell due to a technical correction, but market sentiment was stable, brokers said.
The A index shed 4.406 points or 0.35 percent to 1,251.866 points on volume of 328.337 million shares worth 3.406 billion yuan.
Shanghai's SSE30 blue chip index rose 20.672 points or 0.55 percent to 3,748.033 points.
Shenzhen's hard currency B share index closed slightly higher on Tuesday, with technical charts showing the market had limited downside at current levels, brokers said.
The index edged up 0.56 points or 0.43 percent to 131.45 on turnover of HK$34 million against Monday's HK$45 million.
The domestic A share index lost 0.76 points or 0.18 percent to 413.23 on turnover of 4.1 billion yuan against 5.2 billion in the previous session.
"Technically speaking, the B share index seems to have bottomed out," an analyst at Everbright Securities said.
Further advances in television tube maker Shenzhen SEG helped buoy the B share index, the Everbright analyst said.
SEG, the best B share performer, soared HK$0.41 or 7.75 percent to HK$5.70 on volume of 1.3 million shares. It was the day's second most actively traded issue.
Analysts said SEG was targeted by some foreign institutional bargain hunters after recent losses.
Bengang Steel Plates was the most actively traded B share issue on volume of 2.0 million shares, falling HK$0.01 to HK$2.12 against a recent offer price of HK$2.38 per share.
